info.title: QuickCommands Server
info.description: Cloud save and store for QuickCommands. Authenticate with a Firebase ID token (Bearer).

get.summary: Reports, newest first (open ones by default).

post.summary: Removes a package; its open reports count as upheld.
Makes a hidden or removed package active again; its open reports are dismissed.
Bans a user; optionally removes all their packages.

get.summary: The fixed list of store categories.
The current document exactly as it was saved.

put.summary: Saves a new revision. Requires If-Match: "<revision>" or, for the first save, If-None-Match: *.

delete.summary: Turns cloud save off: all revisions are deleted.

get.summary: Metadata of the stored revisions, newest first (at most 10).
The content of an older revision. To restore it, PUT it again as a new revision.
Liveness and database check for Docker, nginx and monitoring.
The profile of the signed-in user.

put.summary: Sets or changes the public handle (required before publishing).

delete.summary: Deletes cloud save, stars, installs and reports; own packages become tombstones.

get.summary: Own packages in every state except deleted.

post.summary: Publishes a new package (a handle is required).

get.summary: Update check for installed packages: status and version per known ID (unknown IDs are left out).

put.summary: Replaces title, description, category, tags and commands; increases the version.

delete.summary: Deletes the package (author or admin). A tombstone stays for the update check.

post.summary: Counts an installation – once per user and package.
Reports the package. From 3 open reports it is hidden until an admin decides.

oneOf.description: If set, all active or hidden packages of the user are removed with this reason.
The desktop parameter list (JSON array). Stored as-is.

starredByMe.description: Only set for authenticated requests (like InstalledByMe).

PackageRequest.description: Publishing and editing use the same shape: an edit replaces everything.

ShellLanguage.description: Same values as the desktop app's ShellLanguage.
